There is also an obstruction after imposing determinant one. Retain the central level before specialization, and consider completions containing the unextended divided algebra densely, with continuous partial coproducts and compatible continuous actions on vacuum tensor products through three factors. At every nonzero vacuum level cc, no normalized internal two-cocycle in this class compares the two coproducts. A diagonal-current endomorphism of a grouped vacuum pair must commute with the completed action, while the forced first twist coefficient acts through separate translations and violates that commutation. Using the numerator of the Sugawara operator proves the obstruction also at c=−1c=-1, where the usual denominator for the grouped level vanishes.

This obstruction does not decide the same completion problem at c=0c=0. It also leaves the translation-extension twist intact: adjoining dd changes the commutant used by the obstruction. The two statements distinguish an explicit comparison in an enlarged Hopf algebra from a prohibited internal comparison in the specified unextended completions.

19Spectral recognition

Spectral recognition separates a linear fibre, its tensor structure and its Laurent exchange

A category of representations can carry a spectral exchange before a Hopf algebra presenting it has been constructed. Recognition asks for an exact faithful functor to finite-dimensional vector spaces, a coherent tensor comparison, and an additive frame for translation which makes the exchange Laurent polynomial on each pair. Each is substantive data.

Work over an algebraically closed field kk of characteristic zero. Let 𝒞\mathcal C be an essentially small kk-linear abelian rigid tensor category with exact tensor product, finite-dimensional Hom spaces, finite-length objects and simple unit 𝟏\mathbf1, with End⁡(𝟏)=k\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k. Its formal additive monoidal translation τu\tau_u is specified at compatible flat finite parameter stages. A spectral symmetry has maps σX,Y(z):τzX⊗Y⟶Y⊗τzX\sigma_{X,Y}(z):\tau_zX\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes\tau_zX with finite pole order on each pair, satisfying both tensor hexagons, the unit identity, both translation identities and inverse unitarity. The associator and translation tensor maps enter these identities. Only formal parameter directions are completed; the tensor products of coefficient objects remain ordinary ones.

Weighted injective envelopes give an internal criterion

Let LiL_i represent the simple objects, with L0=𝟏L_0=\mathbf1, and put Nijl=[Li⊗Lj:Ll]N_{ij}^{l}=[L_i\otimes L_j:L_l]. A possible fibre dimension must be a family of positive integers satisfying d0=1,di∨=di,didj=∑lNijldl.d_0=1,\qquad d_{i^\vee}=d_i, \qquad d_id_j=\sum_lN_{ij}^{l}d_l. These equations record tensor multiplicities and duality. For example, sending every simple representation of S3S_3 to a line fails on its two-dimensional simple VV: V⊗V=𝟏⊕︎ϵ⊕︎VV\otimes V=\mathbf1\oplus\epsilon\oplus V would require dimensions one and three to agree. Giving VV dimension two restores the necessary equation.

Let EiE_i be the injective envelope of LiL_i in Ind⁡(𝒞)\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C) and set E=⨁iEi⊕︎di,G(X)=Hom⁡(X,E),F(X)=G(X)∗.E=\bigoplus_iE_i^{\oplus d_i},\qquad G(X)=\operatorname{Hom}(X,E),\qquad F(X)=G(X)^*. Injectivity and a composition series show that FF is exact and faithful, with dim⁡F(X)=∑i[X:Li]di\dim F(X)=\sum_i[X:L_i]d_i. Every exact faithful finite-dimensional linear fibre has this form for its simple dimensions.

Theorem

The translated spectral category admits a compatible Laurent presentation if and only if some integral dimension profile admits the following structures on its weighted injective envelope:

  1. A unital associative multiplication μ:E⊗E→E\mu:E\otimes E\to E for which G(Li)⊗G(Lj)⟶G(Li⊗Lj),f⊗g⟼μ(f⊗g),G(L_i)\otimes G(L_j)\longrightarrow G(L_i\otimes L_j), \qquad f\otimes g\longmapsto\mu(f\otimes g), is invertible for every pair of simples.
  2. A unital algebra splitting of the first translation extension 0⟶E⟶J1(E)⟶E⟶0.0\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow J_1(E)\longrightarrow E \longrightarrow0.
  3. Finite Laurent support for the transported spectral exchange on every pair of finite subobjects of EE.

The first condition constructs the tensorator: exactness extends invertibility from simple pairs to all pairs, and the dual inverses of these product maps give F(X)⊗F(Y)≃F(X⊗Y)F(X)\otimes F(Y)\simeq F(X\otimes Y). Associativity of μ\mu is precisely its tensor coherence.

The second condition has an explicit obstruction. A unit-preserving linear splitting q0q_0 of the first-jet extension has multiplication defect BμB_\mu, a normalized internal Hochschild two-cocycle. Replacing q0q_0 by q0+jaq_0+ja changes the defect to Bμ−δμaB_\mu-\delta_\mu a. The equation δμa=Bμ\delta_\mu a=B_\mu therefore produces an algebra splitting. Iteration over independent square-zero parameters and descent along their symmetric invariants integrate it to an additive monoidal translation frame at every finite stage.

The third condition tests both ends of the Laurent support, with a bound allowed to depend on the pair. Every object embeds into a finite direct sum of finite subobjects of EE; naturality then propagates their Laurent bounds to all objects. The resulting coend, formed from matrix coefficients of FF modulo their naturality relations, is an ordinary uncompleted Hopf algebra. Differentiating the frame gives its translation derivation and coderivation, and the transported exchange gives its spectral form. Conversely, a presentation supplies each of the displayed structures. This is a necessary-and-sufficient criterion without an auxiliary ordinary braiding; it does not assert automatic solvability of the equations.

Locally finite translation on extensions forces regularity

There is a useful sufficient test when the unit is the only simple object. Translation acts on V=Ext𝒞1⁡(𝟏,𝟏).V=\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1,\mathbf1). Let DD be its infinitesimal action. Local finiteness means that the span of v,Dv,D2v,…v,Dv,D^2v,\ldots is finite-dimensional for every extension class vv.

Under this hypothesis every spectral exchange is regular at z=0z=0. Evaluation gives a symmetric braiding cX,Y=σX,Y(0)c_{X,Y}=\sigma_{X,Y}(0) preserved by translation. The category has a compatible presentation by a connected commutative Hopf algebra with constant spectral form ρz(b,a)=ε(b)ε(a).\rho_z(b,a)=\varepsilon(b)\varepsilon(a). In particular, finite-dimensionality of the entire extension space is sufficient.

The proof first constructs a linear additive frame, without assuming tensor coherence. Its coend is a connected coalgebra HH whose primitive subspace is VV, and whose translation coderivation restricts to DD. The coradical filtration satisfies Hn/Hn−1↪V⊗n.H_n/H_{n-1}\hookrightarrow V^{\otimes n}. Local finiteness therefore propagates from VV to every coefficient of HH. Every finite coefficient coalgebra lies in a finite translation-stable one. If dim⁡V=d\dim V=d, one also obtains dim⁡Hn≤∑j=0ndj\dim H_n\leq\sum_{j=0}^nd^j.

On two such finite coefficient coalgebras, the exchange is represented by a single finite-dimensional operator R(z)R(z) satisfying R′(z)=AR(z)R'(z)=AR(z) for a constant linear operator AA. A leading pole z−rR−rz^{-r}R_{-r} would produce −rz−r−1R−r-rz^{-r-1}R_{-r} on the left, with no term of that order on the right. Characteristic zero excludes it. The spectral identities can now be evaluated at zero; the symmetric-fibre construction supplies the monoidal frame and Hopf presentation.

The argument does not require commutative coefficient-operator algebras. For instance, the coordinate Hopf algebra k[x,y,w]k[x,y,w] with x,yx,y primitive and Δw=w⊗1+1⊗w+x⊗y\Delta w=w\otimes1+1\otimes w+x\otimes y is commutative but not cocommutative, and its finite dual operator algebras can be noncommutative. Its unit extension space is spanned by x,yx,y.

A genuine pole instead forces an extension class with linearly independent successive translates. This does not obstruct a Laurent presentation. The primitive-current algebra k[x0,x1,…]k[x_0,x_1,\ldots], with Txi=xi+1Tx_i=x_{i+1}, has such an orbit and admits the kernel Gz(xm,xn)=(−1)n∂zm+n(c/z)G_z(x_m,x_n)=(-1)^n\partial_z^{m+n}(c/z) for c≠0c\ne0. Local finiteness is a regularity criterion, not a necessary condition for presentation.

Internal operator images can extract a braiding from a pole

Suppose the simple objects are either the unit alone or the unit and an invertible parity object Π\Pi, with a fixed coherent simple tensor skeleton. Assume the spectral symmetry on that skeleton is the ordinary sign. The injective envelopes construct an exact faithful linear functor FF with dim⁡F(X)=length⁡(X)\dim F(X)=\operatorname{length}(X), binary comparisons jj, and an additive linear translation frame vv.

These comparisons need not yet be monoidal. Let Φ\Phi be the actual matrix of the associator in the jj coordinates, and let KuK_u be the tensor defect of the translation frame. Transport the spectral symmetry with j,vj,v, and remove the Koszul flip PP to obtain an endomorphism RX,Y(z)R_{X,Y}(z) of F(X)⊗F(Y)F(X)\otimes F(Y).

Three image conditions suffice:

  1. The reference transposition jY,XPjX,Y−1j_{Y,X}Pj_{X,Y}^{-1} is the image under FF of an internal morphism of 𝒞\mathcal C.
  2. Each Laurent coefficient of jX,YR(z)jX,Y−1j_{X,Y}R(z)j_{X,Y}^{-1} is the image of an internal endomorphism, including translated inputs and every finite scalar stage.
  3. In every finite structural diagram, all required placements of R,Φ,KR,\Phi,K and their inverses lie in a common finite-dimensional commutative local algebra of even operators. Their residues are the identity, and finite-stage parameters lie in its nilpotent radical.

These conditions concern the given maps and their actual Hom images. They do not require all extension operators in the category to commute.

The nilpotent radical makes logarithm and exponential finite. Define CX,Y=exp⁡([z0]log⁡RX,Y(z)),F(cX,Y)=jY,XPX,YCX,YjX,Y−1.C_{X,Y}=\exp\bigl([z^0]\log R_{X,Y}(z)\bigr), \qquad F(c_{X,Y})=j_{Y,X}P_{X,Y}C_{X,Y}j_{X,Y}^{-1}. The image conditions make cc an internal morphism. Constant-log extraction is multiplicative in a common commutative local algebra, so applying it to both spectral hexagons retains the two associator contributions and gives both ordinary hexagons for cc. Inverse unitarity gives symmetry. Applying it to simultaneous translation retains the KuK_u terms and proves that translation preserves this braiding.

The construction uses the Laurent germ at zero and does not evaluate the exchange at infinity. Independence under a change of coordinates holds when both choices and their comparison matrices lie in common commutative local structural algebras. Arbitrary noncommuting changes are outside that assertion. A natural internal involution alone is insufficient: it can fail a hexagon for the original associator even when its square is one.

An auxiliary symmetry and moderate growth give Laurent normalization

More generally, suppose 𝒞\mathcal C has an auxiliary symmetric braiding preserved by its monoidal translations. No specialization relation to the spectral symmetry is required. Then a compatible Laurent presentation exists exactly when every object has moderate growth, length⁡(X⊗n)≤CXn\operatorname{length}(X^{\otimes n})\leq C_X^n for some CXC_X and all nn. Necessity follows from the dimensions of any faithful fibre. For sufficiency, the symmetric fibre theorem gives finite super vector spaces and an additive monoidal translation frame.

After removing the super flip csc^s, write the exchange as R(z)R(z). Both hexagons, naturality for the auxiliary braiding and independent-parameter translation show that its coefficients generate a finite-dimensional commutative algebra on each pair. In that algebra there is a canonical factorization R(z)=CzBexp⁡(L−+L+).R(z)=Cz^B\exp(L^-+L^+). On each residue-field component, CC is the nonzero leading coefficient and BB is the integer valuation. The polar part L−L^- has nilpotent coefficients, while L+∈A[[z]]L^+\in A[[z]] has nilpotent constant term. The expression uses integer powers of zz and requires no logarithm of zz or of a scalar constant.

The natural tensor change JX,Y=exp⁡(−LX,Y+(0)/2)J_{X,Y}=\exp\bigl(-L^+_{X,Y}(0)/2\bigr) satisfies the tensor coherence equation. Translation turns this constant correction into the full regular exponential. The new transported exchange is σ~X,Y(z)=csCzBexp⁡L−(z).\widetilde\sigma_{X,Y}(z)=c^sCz^B\exp L^-(z). If the radical has nilpotence exponent dd, the polar logarithm has order pp, and the least and greatest residue valuations are bmin⁡,bmax⁡b_{\min},b_{\max}, its powers lie in the finite interval [bmin⁡−(d−1)p, bmax⁡].[b_{\min}-(d-1)p,\ b_{\max}]. The underlying exact faithful functor and additive frame stay fixed. The tensor change need not be internal to 𝒞\mathcal C, and its reconstructed Hopf multiplication can change. It is therefore a monoidal comparison, not an asserted internal twist of a prescribed Hopf algebra.

Odd operators and associators distinguish the hypotheses

Finite supermodules with finitely many odd anticommuting current operators did_i give a polar example. Translation at precision umu^m has mode support at most NX+m−1N_X+m-1 when the original object has support NXN_X; there is no uniform bound over all parameter stages. Even products of the odd operators give a Laurent-polynomial spectral exchange. On the smallest object with ee even, ff odd and d0f=ed_0f=e, it is σ(z)(f⊗f)=−f⊗f−κz−2e⊗e.\sigma(z)(f\otimes f)=-f\otimes f-\kappa z^{-2}e\otimes e. Its double pole is nonzero, although every ordinary natural tensor derivation consisting of even internal maps vanishes. Constant-log extraction gives the Koszul flip. Thus vanishing of ordinary tensor derivations excludes neither this pole nor its Laurent fibre.

Central structural operators can also commute while other extension operators do not. Their extracted braiding retains the constant term of the logarithm; discarding it together with the polar terms changes the result. After a tensor modification, even the reference internal flip can fail a hexagon. The extracted correction then restores both associator contributions and the translation tensorator identity.

The general weighted-envelope criterion remains available beyond these sufficient classes. Constructing its solutions when internal transposition fails or the relevant structural images are noncommutative remains a substantive problem. Over a complete local coefficient ring, compatible finite-projective fibres and effectivity of their coends require additional arguments. The field-valued criteria do not establish those adic conclusions.

20Boundary coring

A boundary detects the coring through its full endomorphism complex

A change of algebra can alter the endomorphisms of a boundary. The exact defect is obtained by applying the boundary to the derived coring of that change. This gives a concrete test for the boundary, including composition, while leaving the question of whether it generates all modules separate.

Let θ:G→R\theta:G\to R be a unital map of differential graded algebras over a field, and let P,QP,Q be right RR-modules. Define the RR-bimodules T=R⊗G𝕃R,F=fib⁡(μ:T→R),T=R\otimes_G^{\mathbb L}R, \qquad F=\operatorname{fib}(\mu:T\to R), where μ\mu is multiplication. The fibre is Cone⁡(μ)[−1]\operatorname{Cone}(\mu)[-1]. All Hom complexes below are derived.

Theorem

Restriction along θ\theta satisfies RHomG⁡(Res⁡P,Res⁡Q)≃RHomR⁡(P⊗R𝕃T,Q),\operatorname{RHom}_G(\operatorname{Res}P,\operatorname{Res}Q) \simeq\operatorname{RHom}_R(P\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}T,Q), and its defect is Cone⁡(RHomR⁡(P,Q)⟶RHomG⁡(Res⁡P,Res⁡Q))≃RHomR⁡(P⊗R𝕃F,Q).\operatorname{Cone}\!\left( \operatorname{RHom}_R(P,Q)\longrightarrow \operatorname{RHom}_G(\operatorname{Res}P,\operatorname{Res}Q) \right) \simeq\operatorname{RHom}_R(P\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}F,Q). In particular, restriction preserves all derived self-endomorphisms of PP exactly when the last complex with Q=PQ=P is acyclic.

Extension–restriction adjunction identifies the first expression with RHomR⁡(P⊗G𝕃R,Q)\operatorname{RHom}_R(P\otimes_G^{\mathbb L}R,Q). Associativity of relative tensor product identifies its input with P⊗R𝕃TP\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}T. Under this adjunction, restriction is precomposition with 1P⊗μ1_P\otimes\mu. Tensoring the fibre sequence F→T→RF\to T\to R with PP and applying RHomR⁡(−,Q)\operatorname{RHom}_R(-,Q) gives the stated cone formula, including the shift.

The formula tests the chosen boundary. A nonzero FF need not remain nonzero after tensoring with PP and mapping back to PP. Conversely, agreement on a vacuum vector tests less than acyclicity of this full mapping complex. The same argument applies to internal Hom in a closed stable coefficient category when the required relative tensors and adjunction exist. A continuous version requires those functors in the specified topological category.

The coproduct retains composition

The object TT is a relative coring: its coproduct takes values in T⊗R𝕃TT\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}T, and its counit is μ\mu. In a two-sided bar model, the coproduct retains every cut, including both extreme cuts: Δ(r0[g1|⋯|gn]r1)=∑i=0n(r0[g1|⋯|gi]1)⊗R(1[gi+1|⋯|gn]r1).\Delta\bigl(r_0[g_1|\cdots|g_n]r_1\bigr) =\sum_{i=0}^n (r_0[g_1|\cdots|g_i]1)\otimes_R (1[g_{i+1}|\cdots|g_n]r_1). The common multibar represents the derived relative tensor, with the totalization and Koszul signs for differential graded inputs. At a cut through a multiplication face, the two middle endpoint terms cancel after balancing over RR. This proves compatibility with the bar differential. Iterating the coproduct enumerates the same weak multicuts in every order.

If f:P⊗R𝕃T→Qf:P\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}T\to Q and g:Q⊗R𝕃T→Wg:Q\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}T\to W represent two restricted maps, their composite is P⊗R𝕃T→1⊗ΔP⊗R𝕃T⊗R𝕃T→f⊗1Q⊗R𝕃T→gW.P\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}T \xrightarrow{1\otimes\Delta} P\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}T\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}T \xrightarrow{f\otimes1}Q\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}T \xrightarrow{g}W. The counit represents the identity. The comparison therefore retains the derived associative endomorphism structure, including coherent composition.

For a concrete shift check, take G=kG=k, R=k[x]R=k[x], and P=Q=kP=Q=k at x=0x=0. Then T=k[xℓ,xr],F=(xℓ−xr)k[xℓ,xr].T=k[x_\ell,x_r],\qquad F=(x_\ell-x_r)k[x_\ell,x_r]. The ideal is free of rank one over the two-variable ring. After tensoring its left endpoint with kk, it is free of rank one as a right RR-module. Consequently RHomR⁡(P⊗R𝕃F,P)=k\operatorname{RHom}_R(P\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}F,P)=k in degree zero. This agrees with the cone of restriction from ExtR∙⁡(k,k)=Λ(ξ)\operatorname{Ext}_R^\bullet(k,k)=\Lambda(\xi), |ξ|=1|\xi|=1, to kk: restriction kills the degree-one class, which appears in degree zero in its cone.

A composite action has two coupled defects

Suppose additional data give a unital map a:H→Ea:H\to E and an equivalence E≃REndR⁡(P)E\simeq\operatorname{REnd}_R(P) induced by a commuting left action on a specified resolution of PP. They define κ:H⟶E≃REndR⁡(P)⟶REndG⁡(Res⁡P).\kappa:H\longrightarrow E\simeq\operatorname{REnd}_R(P) \longrightarrow\operatorname{REnd}_G(\operatorname{Res}P). The octahedral triangle for this composite is Cone⁡(a)⟶Cone⁡(κ)⟶RHomR⁡(P⊗R𝕃F,P)⟶Cone⁡(a)[1].\operatorname{Cone}(a)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cone}(\kappa) \longrightarrow\operatorname{RHom}_R(P\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}F,P) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Cone}(a)[1]. If aa is an equivalence, acyclicity of the boundary detector is the exact criterion for κ\kappa to be an equivalence. Without that hypothesis, the two outer defects are linked by the connecting map; their separate nonvanishing does not force the middle cone to be nonzero.

For a current and ghost realization, the needed extra data are an actual commuting action on an independently specified boundary resolution. Its maps must preserve the prescribed singular fields, collision supports, residues, vacuum actions and continuity. The abstract coring construction determines how to test such an action once supplied; it does not construct that marked action from a match of underlying coefficients.

The boundary generates a specified module sector

Let PP be a homotopically projective right AA-module and put EP=EndA⁡(P)E_P=\operatorname{End}_A(P). The covariant functor RHomA⁡(P,−)\operatorname{RHom}_A(P,-) gives thickA⁡(P)≃Perf⁡(EP).\operatorname{thick}_A(P)\simeq\operatorname{Perf}(E_P). The left side is the closure of PP under finite cones, shifts and retracts; the right side is the corresponding closure of the regular right EPE_P-module. The equivalence extends to all derived modules when PP is a compact generator: compactness makes Hom from PP preserve coproducts, and generation makes its tests conservative.

The generator condition has a simple failure. For A=k[x]A=k[x] and P=kP=k, the nonzero module k[x,x−1]k[x,x^{-1}] has RHomk[x]⁡(k,k[x,x−1])≃[k[x,x−1]→xk[x,x−1]]≃0.\operatorname{RHom}_{k[x]}(k,k[x,x^{-1}]) \simeq[k[x,x^{-1}]\xrightarrow{x}k[x,x^{-1}]]\simeq0. Thus this boundary misses an entire nonzero module. The coring detector decides whether restriction changes its endomorphisms; the generator condition decides how much of the ambient module category those endomorphisms recover. Both questions are distinct from the contravariant coefficient duality and its pro-perfect recipient.

21Polynomial current transfer

A small current resolution deforms with all its higher operations

Eliminating a contractible pair of generators can create a higher operation in the remaining generators. A useful deformation theorem must therefore lift both the differential and the map comparing the small algebra with the original one. Requiring only that the new differential square to zero misses the second condition.

Let kk be a characteristic-zero field, S=k[τ,κ]S=k[\tau,\kappa], and H=k[z]H=k[z]. Give τ,κ\tau,\kappa weights one and two, respectively, and give HH weight zero. In the free algebra over HSH_S, the symbols have independent left and right HSH_S-coefficients; they are not required to commute with zz. Consider BS=HS⟨x,y,v,u,r⟩,|x|=|y|=|v|=0,|u|=|r|=−1,B_S=H_S\langle x,y,v,u,r\rangle, \qquad |x|=|y|=|v|=0,\quad |u|=|r|=-1, with dx=dy=dv=0,du=v−κxy,dr=xv−τ3κz.dx=dy=dv=0,\qquad du=v-\kappa xy, \qquad dr=xv-\tau^3\kappa z. The weights of x,y,u,v,rx,y,u,v,r are 1,1,4,4,51,1,4,4,5, so this differential preserves total weight. The polynomial changes of generators v′=v−κxyv'=v-\kappa xy and ρ=r−xu\rho=r-xu give du=v′,dv′=0,dρ=κx2y−τ3κz.du=v',\qquad dv'=0,\qquad d\rho=\kappa x^2y-\tau^3\kappa z. The pair (u,v′)(u,v') is contractible. Contracting its first occurrence in each word gives a deformation retraction onto RS=HS⟨x,y,ρ⟩,Dρ=κx2y−τ3κz.R_S=H_S\langle x,y,\rho\rangle, \qquad D\rho=\kappa x^2y-\tau^3\kappa z. The inclusion sends ρ\rho to r−xur-xu, and the algebra retraction sends uu to zero, vv to κxy\kappa xy, and rr to ρ\rho. These formulas survive every parameter specialization.

Deleting the cubic term κx2y\kappa x^2y leaves a square-zero differential, but the proposed comparison is no longer a chain map: its defect on rr is exactly κx2y\kappa x^2y. After z=0z=0 and τ=κ=1\tau=\kappa=1, the correct small algebra has H0(R)=k⟨x,y⟩/(x2y),H^0(R)=k\langle x,y\rangle/(x^2y), whereas the truncated differential gives the free algebra k⟨x,y⟩k\langle x,y\rangle. The higher term changes the algebra being resolved.

Positive weights make the lift polynomial

Now let HH be a differential graded algebra of weight zero, and let R0=(THV,d0),V=⨁w≥1Vw,R_0=(T_HV,d_0),\qquad V=\bigoplus_{w\geq1}V_w, be a relative tensor algebra with weight-preserving differential. Assume each weight of VV is projective as a graded HH-bimodule. Its relative cotangent bimodule is ΩR0/H1=R0⊗HV⊗HR0,\Omega^1_{R_0/H}=R_0\otimes_HV\otimes_HR_0, with differential determined by the universal derivation. Require this complex to be semiprojective: its mapping complex must preserve weightwise quasi-isomorphisms in each homogeneous weight of maps. Projectivity of its individual terms is a weaker condition.

Suppose a weight-preserving quasi-isomorphism f0:R0→B0f_0:R_0\to B_0 is given under HH. Let BSB_S be a nonnegatively weighted differential graded algebra under HSH_S, flat in every cochain degree as a graded SS-module, with reduction BS/(τ,κ)=B0B_S/(\tau,\kappa)=B_0.

Theorem

There is a weight-preserving differential DD on THS(V⊗kS)T_{H_S}(V\otimes_kS) and an algebra quasi-isomorphism f:(THS(V⊗kS),D)⟶BSf:(T_{H_S}(V\otimes_kS),D)\longrightarrow B_S reducing to f0f_0. On an input of current weight ww, a parameter correction τaκb\tau^a\kappa^b can occur only if a+2b≤wa+2b\leq w. The construction is polynomial. Both complexes are KK-flat over SS, and ff remains a quasi-isomorphism after extension to every commutative SS-algebra.

Proof

The relative cotangent module represents derivations. Its semiprojectivity makes the map p:DerH⁡(R0,R0)⟶Derf0,H⁡(R0,B0)p:\operatorname{Der}_H(R_0,R_0) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Der}_{f_0,H}(R_0,B_0) a quasi-isomorphism in every mapping weight. Its mapping fibre is therefore acyclic and, over kk, admits a contraction in each weight.

Suppose the differential and algebra map have been lifted modulo (τ,κ)n(\tau,\kappa)^n. Arbitrary generator lifts to the next parameter layer have two defects: F=D~2,G=dBSf~−f~D~.F=\widetilde D^2,\qquad G=d_{B_S}\widetilde f-\widetilde f\widetilde D. The identities for these defects make (F,−G)(F,-G) a cycle in that mapping fibre. Applying its contraction supplies corrections to both D~\widetilde D and f~\widetilde f which kill both defects in the square-zero parameter layer.

A coefficient τaκb\tau^a\kappa^b lowers current weight by a+2ba+2b. Nonnegative weights force it to vanish when this exceeds the input weight. Thus the successive corrections define polynomials, and the parameter filtration is finite in every total weight. Its comparison layers are copies of f0f_0, proving the quasi-isomorphism. The graded-flat modules admit graded-free presentations; filtration by the weights of their basis lifts has associated graded complex given by scalar extension from kk. These filtrations prove KK-flatness, so ordinary coefficient extension computes derived extension and preserves the comparison.

KK-flatness means that tensoring with the complex preserves acyclic complexes. It is the property that makes arbitrary coefficient specialization legitimate here, without a cohomological boundedness assumption.

The lifted differential defines a higher relative coring

Assume the classical algebra is augmented over HH. Put C=V[1]C=V[1] and let t:C→Vt:C\to V be the degree-one shift map. A geometric diagram requires a diagram resolution

If the algebras belong to a specified diagram, the free generators and cotangent module must satisfy the projectivity and semiprojectivity conditions in that diagram category. This makes the correction commute with all the diagram maps. Checking each object separately does not establish the condition.

For a diagram with one arrow, take P=(k→0)P=(k\to0). Resolving PP by the projective arrow diagrams (k→1k)(k\xrightarrow{1}k) and (0→k)(0\to k) adds the missing arrow homotopy. Applying the theorem to prescribed geometric currents still requires one flat parameter diagram containing the actual collision, localization, substitution and vacuum maps. A fixed-coefficient free resolution does not by itself identify its generators with that geometric complex, or verify the needed tensor properties when coefficient algebras vary. Recovering a specified strict binary coalgebra is also a further comparison: higher operations must be removed while preserving its binary unshuffle coproduct, central pair map and geometric operations. The polynomial theorem gives the coherent higher structure and its algebra comparison under the stated hypotheses.

Proposition

Let R=k[[ℏ]]R=k[[\hbar]] and let β:B→Z∂norm\beta:B\to Z_\partial^{\mathrm{norm}} be an operation-preserving map whose underlying complexes are derived ℏ\hbar-complete. If its derived reduction modulo ℏ\hbar is an equivalence, then β\beta is an equivalence.

26Formal geometry and reconstruction

Formal bulk geometry requires a comparison with the actual boundary operations

Derived intersections and Hochschild cochains provide concrete geometric models for boundary constructions. Their products, shifts and descent maps must be identified before they give a bulk reconstruction.

For a map of commutative algebras A→BA\to B, the relative derived tensor product B⊗A𝕃BB\otimes_A^{\mathbb L}B carries a BB-coring structure. Its coproduct inserts the middle unit, b0⊗b1⟼b0⊗1⊗b1,b_0\otimes b_1\longmapsto b_0\otimes1\otimes b_1, and its counit multiplies the two factors. Iterating this construction gives the functions on the Čech nerve. For an ordinary faithfully flat map, descent gives an equivalence between AA-modules and BB-modules with compatible descent data.

The quotient of this groupoid recovers the covered target. It need not equal the object space. The two-point cover of a point has one arrow between every ordered pair of objects. Its groupoid quotient is one point.

For two Lagrangian maps into an nn-shifted symplectic space, their derived intersection has a symplectic form of degree n−1n-1. Its tangent complex fits into the triangle 𝕋Z⟶p1∗𝕋L1⊕︎p2∗𝕋L2→df1−df2π∗𝕋M.\mathbb T_Z\longrightarrow p_1^*\mathbb T_{L_1}\oplus p_2^*\mathbb T_{L_2} \xrightarrow{df_1-df_2} \pi^*\mathbb T_M. This triangle supplies no automatic direct-sum splitting. In particular, ambient degree minus two gives intersection degree minus three.

There is a different model for a classical smooth affine algebra BB: HHq(B)=ΛBqDer⁡(B).HH^q(B)=\Lambda_B^q\operatorname{Der}(B). The derivations have cohomological degree one. Resolving the diagonal by its coordinate differences proves the formula and its exterior product. The Gerstenhaber bracket becomes the Schouten bracket of degree minus one. A compatible Batalin–Vilkovisky operator additionally requires cyclic or volume data.

For an arbitrary boundary differential graded algebra, its cohomology need not be smooth or commutative, and its higher operations need not vanish. The absolute quantum example gives a concrete failure of the latter condition. A general formal bulk comparison must therefore construct the appropriate enhanced algebra, continuous Hochschild model and map preserving those higher operations.

The geometric reconstruction problem is to identify the chiral bar with the relative coring, establish the required descent, and compare the bulk operations with the stated Hochschild and symplectic structures. A physical reconstruction must further preserve supported collisions, boundary actions and the prepared state.

27A free reconstruction

A free junction reconstructs two boundary actions

A boundary condition restricts the fields at the edge of a region. Different boundary conditions can have different observable algebras. A junction is the space of fields and operators interpolating between them. Each boundary algebra acts on the junction from its own end.

There is an explicit free example on an interval I=[0,1]I=[0,1] times a complex disk. It is a cotangent theory: the fields occur in conjugate pairs, with a bilinear action. One boundary condition permits the target coordinate to vary over a complex line. The other fixes it at the origin. Denote these boundary conditions by WW and PP.

The quantum construction uses finite polynomial local operators at scalar coupling one. It retains the boundary traces, their normal integrals, their derivatives along the disk, and their differential-form descendants. These choices specify the domain before any endomorphism algebra is computed.

The essential junction has four fields γ,b,β,c\gamma,b,\beta,c, with

Db=γ,Dβ=−c,Dγ=Dc=0.Db=\gamma,\qquad D\beta=-c,\qquad D\gamma=Dc=0.

The fields γ,β\gamma,\beta are even. The fields b,cb,c are odd. Their nonzero contractions are

β(z)γ(w)∼1z−w,γ(z)β(w)∼−1z−w,c(z)b(w)∼1z−w,b(z)c(w)∼1z−w.\begin{aligned} \beta(z)\gamma(w)&\sim\frac1{z-w},& \gamma(z)\beta(w)&\sim-\frac1{z-w},\\ c(z)b(w)&\sim\frac1{z-w},& b(z)c(w)&\sim\frac1{z-w}. \end{aligned}

The endpoint traces are actual restrictions of the bulk fields. Their primitives are integrals along the interval. Thus the relation Db=γDb=\gamma records a boundary coordinate that is the differential of a bulk integral. It is an equation on the fields of the theory.

Taking modes gives the junction complex

M=ℂ[xi,yn]⊗Λ(θi,ηn),i≥0,n≥1,D=∑ixi∂θi−∑nηn∂yn.\begin{aligned} M&=\mathbb C[x_i,y_n]\otimes\Lambda(\theta_i,\eta_n), &&i\geq0,\quad n\geq1,\\ D&=\sum_i x_i\partial_{\theta_i} -\sum_n\eta_n\partial_{y_n}. \end{aligned}

The notation Λ\Lambda denotes the exterior algebra of odd variables. Their degrees are |θi|=−1|\theta_i|=-1 and |ηn|=1|\eta_n|=1. Every vector is a finite polynomial. The two commuting boundary actions are

A=ℂ[xi,pn],pn=∂yn,B=Λ(κi,ηn),κi=∂θi.A=\mathbb C[x_i,p_n], \qquad p_n=\partial_{y_n}, \qquad B=\Lambda(\kappa_i,\eta_n), \qquad \kappa_i=\partial_{\theta_i}.

The regular modes select the completion and the module category. A regular κ\kappa-action is rational when sufficiently high modes kill each vector. A regular pp-action also has a finite cutoff on each vector and is jointly locally nilpotent: sufficiently long products of the remaining modes kill that vector.

The relevant semiderived category retains these regular-mode conditions. It inverts maps whose cones are coacyclic after retaining the regular coalgebra action. Here coacyclic means generated by total complexes of exact sequences, allowing cones, shifts and direct sums. This choice records which acyclic complexes may be discarded.

Theorem

On this polynomial junction and in the stated semiderived categories, the actual two boundary actions induce quasi-isomorphisms

Aˆ≃𝐑EndB⁡(M),Bˆ≃𝐑EndA⁡(M).\widehat A\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{End}_{B}(M), \qquad \widehat B\simeq\mathbf R\operatorname{End}_{A}(M).

The completion Aˆ\widehat A has finite polynomial output in each regular-mode row. The completion Bˆ\widehat B has finite exterior output in each such row. The maps preserve the unit and ordinary holomorphic translation.

Proof

The normal integral variables outside the four-field junction occur in contractible pairs. Their contractions with the junction vanish, so an Euler homotopy removes them while preserving both boundary actions.

For the even action, the remaining mapping complex is

Homℂ⁡(ℂ[yn],ℂ[xi]).\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C} \bigl(\mathbb C[y_n],\mathbb C[x_i]\bigr).

An operator ∑βfβ(x)∂yβ\sum_\beta f_\beta(x)\partial_y^\beta, followed by evaluation at y=0y=0, sends the monomial yγy^\gamma to γ!fγ(x)\gamma!f_\gamma(x). This identifies every polynomial-output row. The free bar resolution on the multiplying modes and the cofree resolution on the regular modes compute this mapping complex in the stated localization.

For the exterior action the mapping complex is Homℂ⁡(Λ(θi),Λ(ηn))\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(\Lambda(\theta_i),\Lambda(\eta_n)). Ordered exterior derivatives extract its rows with their signs. In both cases the original action map preserves composition, so the comparisons identify differential graded algebras.

The category is essential to the result. With one regular odd mode, the corresponding ordinary resolution changes a polynomial endomorphism space ℂ[x]\mathbb C[x] into a power-series space ℂ[[s]]\mathbb C[[s]]. That resolution is an ordinary quasi-isomorphism but is excluded by the semiderived weak equivalences. The two endomorphism calculations therefore answer different questions.

Sewing retains the fields at the join

Sewing joins intervals by matching their boundary data. To remove an internal boundary condition, the free theory adds an independent conjugate pair of fields at the join. Its coupling is specified in the action.

For W→P→WW\to P\to W, an even pair (π,t)(\pi,t) couples to the difference of the two point-boundary traces. The resulting differential includes

Dt=c1−c2,Db1=γ1+π,Db2=−γ2−π.Dt=c_1-c_2,\qquad Db_1=\gamma_1+\pi,\qquad Db_2=-\gamma_2-\pi.

The surviving closed pair is

γres=−π,βres=t+β1+β2,βres(z)γres(w)∼1z−w.\gamma_{\mathrm{res}}=-\pi, \qquad \beta_{\mathrm{res}}=t+\beta_1+\beta_2, \qquad \beta_{\mathrm{res}}(z)\gamma_{\mathrm{res}}(w) \sim\frac1{z-w}.

These are precisely the even residual fields on the uncut W→WW\to W interval. A P→W→PP\to W\to P sewing instead leaves an odd bcbc pair. Retaining the point boundary at the join would remove the constant even mode. The conjugate seam fields are therefore part of the reconstruction.

For any finite alternating chain, one cotangent incidence complex describes all joins simultaneously. Its contractible complement can be removed by a pairing-compatible homotopy. Every parenthesization uses the same coupled complex, differential and exterior actions. This proves finite interval sewing on the specified free polynomial domain.

The interacting problem requires the corresponding construction from its full coupled action, including supported contact terms and the choice of physical state.

28Mixed theories and obstructions

Compatible corrections must solve the coupled equations at every scale

A bulk theory can act on a boundary theory, and the boundary operators can compose. Deforming these three structures together requires the action to remain compatible with composition. Even if the bulk and boundary equations can each be solved, their compatibility equation can have an obstruction. The mixed holomorphic–topological problem asks for all these equations at once: holomorphic dependence in the complex directions, topological dependence in the transverse directions, and compatible operations where local descriptions overlap.

A differential graded Lie algebra packages a deformation problem into a cochain complex with a bracket of degree zero. Its differential DD and bracket obey the graded derivation and Jacobi identities. A degree-one element aa specifies a consistent deformation when its curvature vanishes: Curv⁡(a)=Da+12[a,a]=0.\operatorname{Curv}(a)=Da+\frac12[a,a]=0. This is the Maurer–Cartan equation. A descending filtration F1T⊃F2T⊃⋯F^1T\supset F^2T\supset\cdots records the order of corrections. The required assumptions are that DD preserves the filtration, brackets add filtration orders, and TT is the inverse limit of its quotients with no nonzero element invisible in every quotient.

Over a field of characteristic zero, local deformation complexes with compatible face maps have an explicit total carrier. Attach polynomial differential forms on a simplex to every multiple overlap and require their restrictions to agree on its faces. Completing this Thom–Whitney totalization in the filtration retains the bracket, its signs, and the overlap equations. These conditions make the total carrier complete and make its maps to the finite quotients surjective in every degree.

Theorem

For a partial solution ar−1a_{r-1} modulo FrTF^rT, the curvature of any lift defines a well-defined obstruction or(ar−1)∈H2(FrT/Fr+1T,D).o_r(a_{r-1})\in H^2(F^rT/F^{r+1}T,D). It vanishes exactly when that partial solution extends modulo Fr+1TF^{r+1}T. A compatible sequence of such extensions determines a unique complete solution.

Proof

The new filtration quotient is central: bracketing it with an element of positive order lands in the next quotient. Consequently a correction bb changes the remaining curvature by exactly DbDb. The differential of the curvature is zero by the Bianchi identity, so the curvature defines the stated cohomology class. Vanishing of this class supplies the correction. Completeness assembles compatible corrections, and separation forces the assembled curvature to vanish.

Compatibility is a mathematical condition on the corrections themselves. For example, an overlap correction can require a polynomial f(t)f(t) satisfying f′(t)=g(t)f'(t)=g(t) and f(0)=f(1)=0f(0)=f(1)=0. A correction exists exactly when ∫01g(t)dt=0\int_0^1g(t)\,dt=0. The case g=1g=1 is locally integrable and has no correction satisfying both face conditions. Its inclusion into unrestricted interval forms is injective on cochains, yet the target admits the forbidden correction f=tf=t. For g=2t−1g=2t-1, the actual permitted correction is f=t2−tf=t^2-t. In the full deformation problem, projected obstruction classes detect the total obstruction when their maps on the relevant cohomology group are jointly injective. An alternative is to construct a primitive satisfying every face equation directly.

The cubic trace decides the local scalar anomaly

A concrete calculation comes from free holomorphic matter on ℂ2\mathbb C^2. Let 𝔤\mathfrak g be an ordinary finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra, and let ρ\rho act on a finite-dimensional complex vector space VV. The fields γ\gamma and β\beta take values in VV and its shifted dual. Their free action is ∫β∂‾γ∧dz1∧dz2\int\beta\bar\partial\gamma\wedge dz_1\wedge dz_2. A compactly supported background AA couples through ∫βρ(A)γ∧dz1∧dz2\int\beta\rho(A)\gamma\wedge dz_1\wedge dz_2.

The background includes all form and ghost components and has total degree one. Its differential is δA=∂‾A−A2\delta A=\bar\partial A-A^2, with the tensor signs determined by that total degree. The scalar quantum anomaly is Θρ(A)=−124π2∫ℂ2TrV⁡[A(∂1A∂2A−∂2A∂1A)]∧dz1∧dz2.\Theta_\rho(A)=-\frac1{24\pi^2}\int_{\mathbb C^2} \operatorname{Tr}_V\!\left[A(\partial_1A\,\partial_2A-\partial_2A\,\partial_1A)\right] \wedge dz_1\wedge dz_2. A scalar correction bb must satisfy δb=−ℏΘρ\delta b=-\hbar\Theta_\rho. Here ℏ\hbar records loop order. A local correction is an integral of a polynomial in fields and finitely many derivatives at the same point. Smooth coordinate-dependent coefficients are allowed, with derivative order bounded on each compact coordinate set. Completion allows infinitely many background orders and nonnegative powers of ℏ\hbar; each fixed coefficient still uses finitely many derivatives.

Theorem

In either the constant-coefficient or the smooth-coefficient local space, the scalar correction exists exactly when TrV⁡ρ(X)3=0for every X∈𝔤.\operatorname{Tr}_V\rho(X)^3=0\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathfrak g. Equivalently, the symmetric trilinear trace tρ(X,Y,Z)=16∑σ∈S3TrV⁡(ρ(Xσ(1))ρ(Xσ(2))ρ(Xσ(3)))t_\rho(X,Y,Z)=\frac16\sum_{\sigma\in S_3} \operatorname{Tr}_V\bigl(\rho(X_{\sigma(1)})\rho(X_{\sigma(2)})\rho(X_{\sigma(3)})\bigr) vanishes, where (X1,X2,X3)=(X,Y,Z)(X_1,X_2,X_3)=(X,Y,Z). No reductivity or semisimplicity assumption is required.

The necessity can be seen by restricting the background to any one-dimensional abelian subalgebra. A local boundary then has an antiholomorphic derivative in its principal symbol, whereas the cubic anomaly retains a nonzero determinant in the holomorphic derivatives. Reducing derivative order extends this obstruction to smooth coefficients. Conversely, polarization of the cubic trace shows that tρ=0t_\rho=0 makes the original anomaly density identically zero, so the zero correction suffices.

The criterion gives explicit examples. For an abelian representation with charges qjq_j, it is ∑jqj3=0\sum_jq_j^3=0. The defining representation of 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 satisfies it. For 𝔰𝔩3\mathfrak{sl}_3, the matrix diag⁡(1,1,−2)\operatorname{diag}(1,1,-2) has cubic trace −6-6 and detects a nonzero local obstruction. A representation and its dual have opposite cubic traces, so their direct sum cancels this scalar anomaly.

Nonlocal corrections and higher transport have explicit formulas

Allowing kernels that couple distinct points changes the correction problem. On flat ℂ2\mathbb C^2, with compact smooth backgrounds and an ordinary finite-dimensional representation, the scalar terms represented by cycle graphs have a large-heat-time limit Ψρ\Psi_\rho. This limit satisfies δΨρ=Θρ.\delta\Psi_\rho=\Theta_\rho. Consequently IL−ℏΨρI_L-\hbar\Psi_\rho solves the scalar curvature equation at every positive heat scale LL, with compatible truncations at every background order. The construction works for every such representation, including those with nonzero cubic trace. Its convergence follows from a uniform bound on a long-time propagator edge; deleting that edge leaves a path whose kernel is integrable against the compact inputs. The primitive belongs to the specified nonlocal space.

A related mixed free theory on ℝ2×ℂ2\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb C^2 gives a direct comparison with scalar observables. Its observables are compact distribution kernels, polynomial in the matter fields at each formal coefficient. Plain evaluation at zero fields fails to commute with the quantum differential: a quadratic observable can contract to a nonzero scalar. The quadratic-interaction and scalar-curvature assumptions are part of this result.

There is also an invertible comparison of the full fluctuation algebras at any two strictly positive heat scales. Recenter Wick transport at a scale-compatible interaction and take its Taylor coefficients. These coefficients form a complete filtered L∞L_\infty isomorphism: the linear map is supplemented by higher maps that preserve the brackets up to specified homotopies. The construction also applies when the common background curvature is a nonzero scalar, since scalar curvature acts trivially by the matter bracket. Compatible nonlinear families are determined by their value at one reference scale. The linear inverse limit acquires a bracket by transport from that reference scale; changing the reference gives a higher isomorphism with linear part equal to the identity. A componentwise heat bracket can fail to preserve compatible families, and a zero-scale limit requires separate renormalization.

The coefficient domain and the binary comparison

The positive-scale model has no boundary. Closure of the actual currents reduces to connected paths

At finite jet order and positive scale, disjoint-region Wick operations act on the actual compact distribution kernels of holomorphic currents. Each current has two matter slots. A connected contraction therefore has the shape of a path, leaving two slots, or a cycle, leaving a scalar. The scalar unit already contains the cycle coefficients.

This gives an exact criterion: the unital algebra generated by the currents is closed under every disjoint operation if and only if every complete signed connected path sum belongs to its quadratic current space. The criterion includes products with several current factors in the same region. A two-region operation can already contain a three-vertex path, so testing pairs of individual generators alone does not exhaust it.

The connected expansion also constructs the minimal enlargement closed under the differential, the quantum contraction, and all disjoint operations. At each stage, adjoin the complete quadratic path sums and close their span under the differential and heat bracket; then take the algebra they generate. The increasing union gives the required enlargement, without completing in the number of fields or in the number of stages. Equality with the original current algebra remains open. A nonzero first-jet descendant is constructed, while a separating functional for one prescribed finite span fails on an allowed current with a one-form input; that separator therefore leaves the full membership question undecided.

The remaining physical comparison has a precise target. It must preserve the original current space under the higher maps, construct the operations as the open sets vary, and prove the required local gluing property. The total obstruction theorem then governs the coupled equations on that carrier. Scalar anomaly cancellation, positive-scale transport, and the connected-path criterion supply explicit parts of this construction; the full mixed bulk–boundary comparison and all its collision compatibilities remain open.

29Cyclic brane couplings

Matrix branes admit explicit coupling corrections with a remaining cubic equation

A brane supplies a boundary condition and its own algebra of open-string observables. In a matrix model for NN coincident branes, two even matrices X,YX,Y describe the positions, while a ghost cc of degree one and a variable ψ\psi of degree minus one retain the gauge symmetry and the equation [X,Y]=0[X,Y]=0 within a complex. The entries of the matrices belong to a graded-commutative coefficient algebra; matrix multiplication remains noncommutative. The differential is QX=−[c,X],QY=−[c,Y],Qc=−c2,Qψ=[X,Y]−[c,ψ].QX=-[c,X],\qquad QY=-[c,Y],\qquad Qc=-c^2, \qquad Q\psi=[X,Y]-[c,\psi]. It squares to zero. A trace polynomial in XX and YY is therefore closed under QQ, and a commutator of the matrices can have a specified primitive involving ψ\psi.

The bulk labels are formal Hamiltonians in two variables q,pq,p, modulo constants, with Poisson bracket {f,g}=fqgp−fpgq\{f,g\}=f_qg_p-f_pg_q. Choose the representative with zero constant term and put each monomial in the order qapbq^ap^b. Its candidate boundary charge is Jf=Tr⁡(XaYb)J_f=\operatorname{Tr}(X^aY^b), extended linearly and coefficientwise. These facts specify the open comparison without discarding the explicit quadratic and supported coupling constructions.

31Residues and compact support

Compact representatives recover the central residue

The free interval example has a controlled operator domain. An interacting boundary theory must also specify which distributions and functional kernels are allowed. Continuity on test fields and rapid decrease of an observable kernel impose different conditions.

A Schwartz field is smooth, with every derivative decreasing faster than any inverse polynomial at infinity. An integral can be continuous on such fields even when its own kernel is translation invariant and fails to decrease. Multiplying by a smooth function of compact support gives a compact kernel, but differentiation then produces terms involving that function.

β=∂z‾η,τ(adz‾)=−1π∫ℂadxdy,z=x+iy.\beta=\partial_{\bar z}\eta, \qquad \tau(a\,d\bar z)=-\frac1\pi\int_{\mathbb C}a\,dx\,dy, \qquad z=x+iy.

The Dolbeault differential is ∂‾f=(∂z‾f)dz‾\bar\partial f=(\partial_{\bar z}f)d\bar z. The form βfdz‾\beta f\,d\bar z has compact support in the annulus whenever ff is a Laurent polynomial.

Proposition

For every Laurent polynomial ff,

τ(βfdz‾)=Resz=0⁡f(z)dz.\tau(\beta f\,d\bar z) =\operatorname{Res}_{z=0} f(z)\,dz.

The map f↦βfdz‾f\mapsto\beta f\,d\bar z has cohomological degree one. Changing η\eta with its boundary values fixed changes this map by an explicit compactly supported Dolbeault homotopy.

Proof

Since ff is holomorphic on the annulus,

d(ηfdz)=2iβfdxdy.d(\eta f\,dz)=2i\beta f\,dx\,dy.

The outer boundary contributes zero. The inner boundary has clockwise induced orientation. Stokes’ theorem therefore gives 2i∫Aβfdxdy=−2πiRes⁡fdz2i\int_A\beta f\,dx\,dy=-2\pi i\operatorname{Res}f\,dz.

For two cutoffs η0,η1\eta_0,\eta_1, their difference has compact support and

(∂z‾η1−∂z‾η0)fdz‾=∂‾((η1−η0)f).(\partial_{\bar z}\eta_1-\partial_{\bar z}\eta_0)f\,d\bar z =\bar\partial\bigl((\eta_1-\eta_0)f\bigr).

This supplies the asserted homotopy.

The degree of the representative is consequential. Choose another compactly supported function ρ\rho, equal to one near the support of β\beta. Define

ωΣ(F,H)=−112π∫ℂ(∂z3F)Hdxdy,ωres(f,h)=112Res⁡f′′′hdz.\omega_\Sigma(F,H) =-\frac1{12\pi}\int_{\mathbb C}(\partial_z^3F)H\,dx\,dy, \qquad \omega_{\mathrm{res}}(f,h) =\frac1{12}\operatorname{Res} f'''h\,dz.

Both mixed pairings recover the Laurent central coefficient:

ωΣ(ρf,βh)=ωΣ(βf,ρh)=ωres(f,h).\omega_\Sigma(\rho f,\beta h) =\omega_\Sigma(\beta f,\rho h) =\omega_{\mathrm{res}}(f,h).

For the first equality, derivatives of ρ\rho vanish near the support of β\beta. For the other order, three integrations by parts transfer the derivatives, including every derivative of β\beta. The residue of a total Laurent derivative is zero.

Writing em=zm+1∂ze_m=z^{m+1}\partial_z, the coefficient is

ωres(em,en)=m3−m12δm+n,0.\omega_{\mathrm{res}}(e_m,e_n) =\frac{m^3-m}{12}\delta_{m+n,0}.

In particular, e2,e−2e_2,e_{-2} give 1/21/2. With both inputs multiplied only by a radial ρ\rho, their smooth pairing is zero. An ordinary cutoff therefore cannot replace the degree-one Dolbeault representative.

The same construction realizes any finite collection of formal normal derivatives by smooth compactly supported fields satisfying the relative boundary conditions. It identifies the corresponding central coefficient functionals. The full nonlinear differential imposes another equation.

For an odd holomorphic ghost cc, with differential Qc=−gc∂zcQc=-g c\,\partial_zc, replacing cc by ρc\rho c gives

∂‾(ρc)=(∂‾ρ)c,−g(ρc)∂z(ρc)+gρc∂zc=gρ(1−ρ)c∂zc.\begin{aligned} \bar\partial(\rho c)&=(\bar\partial\rho)c,\\ -g(\rho c)\partial_z(\rho c)+g\rho c\,\partial_zc &=g\rho(1-\rho)c\,\partial_zc. \end{aligned}

The second expression is nonzero on allowed relative inputs. For example, take c=t(θ0+θ1z)c=t(\theta_0+\theta_1z), where tt is the normal coordinate and θ0,θ1\theta_0,\theta_1 are independent odd coefficients. The defect is gt2ρ(1−ρ)θ0θ1gt^2\rho(1-\rho)\theta_0\theta_1.

Thus the compact representatives recover the central residue, while their extension to a map of nonlinear field complexes requires additional supported homotopies. The quantum comparison must also retain the regulated reflected contraction, its mixed off-diagonal term and its behavior when one interaction is removed.

32A coupled state problem

A rotor history has an explicit relative gauge action

A physical state also needs a Hamiltonian and a time variable. An oriented boundary circle supplies neither a time scale nor an inverse temperature. A positive clock one-form e(θ)dθe(\theta)d\theta supplies that extra datum. Its total length can be fixed to the inverse temperature.

Consider LL rotors taking values in SU(N)SU(N), the group of complex unitary N×NN\times N matrices with determinant one. A rotor history consists of smooth paths gj(θ)g_j(\theta) and momenta Jj(θ)J_j(\theta) in its Lie algebra. Put B(X,Y)=−Tr⁡(XY)B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{Tr}(XY). Let a(θ)a(\theta) be the traceless connection obtained by restricting the boundary field to a chosen point of the complex curve.

The Hamiltonian specifies energy. A rotor Hamiltonian has a quadratic kinetic term and an interaction between adjacent sites,

K0=12ℐ∑jB(Jj,Jj)+V(g),ℐ>0,V(g)=ν∑j[N−ReTr⁡(gj−1gj+1)],ν>0,gL+1=g1.\begin{aligned} K_0&=\frac1{2\mathcal I}\sum_j B(J_j,J_j)+V(g), &&\mathcal I>0,\\ V(g)&=\nu\sum_j \left[N-\operatorname{ReTr}(g_j^{-1}g_{j+1})\right], &&\nu>0,\quad g_{L+1}=g_1. \end{aligned}

An axial chemical charge retains both left and right actions. Fix a real traceless diagonal matrix H0H_0, put A0=iH0A_0=iH_0, and choose background framings χj∈SU(N)\chi_j\in SU(N). For real hh, define

wj=12(Adgj−1⁡A0+Adχj⁡A0),Qax=−∑jB(Jj,wj),Kh=K0−hQax.\begin{aligned} w_j&=\frac12\left( \operatorname{Ad}_{g_j^{-1}}A_0+ \operatorname{Ad}_{\chi_j}A_0\right),\\ Q_{\mathrm{ax}}&=-\sum_j B(J_j,w_j),& K_h&=K_0-hQ_{\mathrm{ax}}. \end{aligned}

Here Adg⁡X=gXg−1\operatorname{Ad}_gX=gXg^{-1}. The framings are prescribed background fields. They transform with the connection.

Under a common gauge transformation u(θ)u(\theta),

gj⟼gju,Jj⟼u−1Jju,a⟼u−1au+u−1u′,χj⟼u−1χj.\begin{aligned} g_j&\longmapsto g_ju,& J_j&\longmapsto u^{-1}J_ju,\\ a&\longmapsto u^{-1}au+u^{-1}u',& \chi_j&\longmapsto u^{-1}\chi_j. \end{aligned}

The action

S0=∫dθ[∑jB(Jj,gj−1gj′−a)−eKh]S_0=\int d\theta\left[ \sum_j B(J_j,g_j^{-1}g'_j-a)-eK_h \right]

is invariant under these transformations. The derivative term in the transformed velocity gj−1gj′g_j^{-1}g'_j cancels the derivative term in the transformed connection. The two terms in the chemical charge transform together.

The Batalin–Vilkovisky, or BV, construction adds conjugate antifields and an odd bracket to encode equations and symmetries. Here the boundary gauge differential remains external. The rotor histories acquire their own odd cotangent variables.

Proposition

With the specified clock, framing and compact real charge, the rotor history defines a relative Batalin–Vilkovisky action over the boundary gauge complex. On a circle its relative master equation vanishes. On an interval its failure is the signed difference of the endpoint gauge charges.

Let γ\gamma be the restricted traceless ghost. The gauge transformations are sgj=gjγsg_j=g_j\gamma, sJj=[Jj,γ]sJ_j=[J_j,\gamma], sa=γ′+[a,γ]sa=\gamma'+[a,\gamma], and sγ=−γ2s\gamma=-\gamma^2. Adding the antifield terms that generate these transformations gives SrelS_{\mathrm{rel}}, with

sextSrel+12(Srel,Srel)=0.s_{\mathrm{ext}}S_{\mathrm{rel}} +\frac12(S_{\mathrm{rel}},S_{\mathrm{rel}})=0.

Gauge invariance proves the term without antifields. Nilpotence of the displayed transformations proves the terms linear in antifields.

The endpoint structure uses an even Hamiltonian bracket, called the BFV bracket. The rotor endpoint potential and charge are

λ=∑jB(Jj,gj−1δgj),Ωrot=∑jB(Jj,γ).\lambda=\sum_j B(J_j,g_j^{-1}\delta g_j), \qquad \Omega_{\mathrm{rot}}=\sum_j B(J_j,\gamma).

With the symplectic convention ωrot=−δλ\omega_{\mathrm{rot}}=-\delta\lambda, cutting the circle to [θ−,θ+][\theta_-,\theta_+] gives

sextSrel+12(Srel,Srel)bulk=−Ωrot(θ+)+Ωrot(θ−).s_{\mathrm{ext}}S_{\mathrm{rel}} +\frac12(S_{\mathrm{rel}},S_{\mathrm{rel}})_{\mathrm{bulk}} =-\Omega_{\mathrm{rot}}(\theta_+) +\Omega_{\mathrm{rot}}(\theta_-).

These terms cancel when intervals are joined with matching endpoint data.

Support distinguishes this construction from other rotor couplings. Varying the connection gives a source integrated along the entire boundary circle. A point source samples finitely many positions. There are smooth allowed variations that vanish at every sampled point but have a nonzero integral against the rotor momentum. Equality of the zero-connection Hamiltonians consequently leaves their field couplings distinct.

The Gibbs state of a specified self-adjoint quantum Hamiltonian has density ρh=Zh−1e−βKh\rho_h=Z_h^{-1}e^{-\beta K_h}, provided the heat operator is trace class and Zh=Tr⁡(e−βKh)Z_h=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta K_h}) is finite. This operator definition gives a thermal state without constructing a path-integral measure.

For holography, the remaining comparison must identify the rotor’s relative symplectic and endpoint data with the actual bulk and boundary theory. It must also map occupied boundary states to closed observables and reproduce the mixed contact terms and response functions. Gauge invariance and a well-defined thermal trace supply parts of that construction.

33Descendants and states

Independent descendant labels admit an invertible quantum state comparison

A partition function records more than a list of local operations. Its coefficients specify states, insertion labels, descendant orders and genus. A reversible comparison must retain those labels separately.

Let VV be a finite-dimensional even vector space over a characteristic-zero field. Fix a nondegenerate symmetric pairing and a distinguished nonzero vector. Choose a basis eαe_\alpha containing that vector, and let eαe^\alpha be its metric-dual basis.

This is an algebra over K[[λ2]]K[[\lambda^2]], with its prescribed stable-weight completion.

The full quantum operator includes a unit translation, a linear transformation and a quadratic contraction. In the descendant variables, the operator is rˆ=∑ℓ≥1[−(rℓ)𝟏μ∂tℓ+1,μ+∑d≥0td,ν(rℓ)νμ∂td+ℓ,μ+ℏ2∑i+j=ℓ−1(−1)i+1(rℓ)μν∂ti,μ∂tj,ν].\widehat r=\sum_{\ell\ge1}\left[ -(r_\ell)_{\mathbf1}{}^\mu\partial_{t_{\ell+1,\mu}} +\sum_{d\ge0}t_{d,\nu}(r_\ell)_\nu{}^\mu \partial_{t_{d+\ell,\mu}} +\frac{\hbar}{2}\sum_{i+j=\ell-1}(-1)^{i+1} (r_\ell)^{\mu\nu} \partial_{t_{i,\mu}}\partial_{t_{j,\nu}} \right]. Repeated state indices are summed. The index 𝟏\mathbf1 denotes the distinguished vector, and the pairing raises the indices in the last term.

Theorem

The map JJ conjugates this entire quantum operator to a continuous operator Dr=JrˆJ−1D_r=J\widehat rJ^{-1} on the specified negative-mode completion. Its exponential is a continuous linear automorphism with inverse e−Dre^{-D_r}, and Jerˆ=eDrJ.Je^{\widehat r}=e^{D_r}J.

Proof

Define the nonnegative deficit δ=3k−w\delta=3k-w. Every nonzero term of index ℓ\ell increases δ\delta by 2ℓ2\ell. The unit term lowers kk by one and removes descendant weight 2ℓ+32\ell+3. The other terms keep kk fixed and remove weight 2ℓ2\ell.

For an output of stable weight kk, only finitely many operator factors can contribute. Its input weights are at most ⌊5k/2⌋\lfloor5k/2\rfloor. Each such input space is finite-dimensional. These bounds justify the exponential, its inverse and the conjugation identity coefficient by coefficient.

The quadratic term makes this a linear quantum action. It need not preserve multiplication. The completion also matters. For one state and r1=1r_1=1, the allowed input λ5q23\lambda^5q_2^3 contributes −λ2-\lambda^2 through three unit derivatives. A rule using only input weights at most the output weight would lose it.

A weaker bound ∑(dj+1)≤3k\sum(d_j+1)\le3k admits ∑k≥0λkq2k\sum_{k\ge0}\lambda^kq_2^k. Under the same exponential, the constant coefficients of its successive partial sums alternate between one and zero. That weaker completion has no resulting formal limit.

A finite nonsemisimple example has explicit tensors in every genus

Consider the eight-dimensional Frobenius algebra A=K[x,y]/(x4,y2),τ(a)=[x3y]a.A=K[x,y]/(x^4,y^2),\qquad \tau(a)=[x^3y]a. Its pairing is η(a,b)=τ(ab)\eta(a,b)=\tau(ab). The chosen loop is additional data. When the two cyclic Hodge differentials vanish, the canonical Hodge propagator vanishes as well. It does not produce this nontrivial loop.

The finite paired construction gives an exact coefficient and operator comparison. Its identification with geometric factorization state spaces still requires their supported operations, polarization, physical parameter normalization and independently constructed partition state.

Collapsing labels can lose information before that comparison. The substitution td,α↦tαsdt_{d,\alpha}\mapsto t_\alpha s_d kills t0,at1,b−t1,at0,b.t_{0,a}t_{1,b}-t_{1,a}t_{0,b}. The specialized generating series remains meaningful, but these variables alone cannot give an inverse coefficient map.

34Pairings and quantum transport

The Todd correction transports the pairing and the distinguished unit

A comparison of state spaces must preserve the pairing used in quantum contractions. On a smooth quartic K3 surface, this requirement can be calculated explicitly.

Let HH be the hyperplane class and pp the point class, with ∫p=1\int p=1. Then H2=4p,td⁡(X)=1+2p,td⁡(X)=1+p.H^2=4p,\qquad \operatorname{td}(X)=1+2p,\qquad \sqrt{\operatorname{td}(X)}=1+p. The Todd class is the characteristic class entering Riemann–Roch. Its square root has inverse 1−p1-p.

For example, ηV(1,1)=2=ηW(1+p,1+p),ηW(1,1)=0.\eta_V(1,1)=2=\eta_W(1+p,1+p), \qquad \eta_W(1,1)=0.

Theorem

If the distinguished vector ee is sent to UeUe, and each operator rℓr_\ell is conjugated to UrℓU−1Ur_\ell U^{-1}, then UˆDr,e=DUrU−1,UeUˆ.\widehat U D_{r,e} =D_{UrU^{-1},Ue}\widehat U. The corresponding exponential actions agree on the full stable completion. Transport of a supplied CohFT preserves its unit and both sewing identities in every genus.

The proof follows separately for the unit derivative, the linear term and the quadratic contraction. For sewing, the inverse pairing transforms by ηW−1=(U⊗U)ηV−1\eta_W^{-1}=(U\otimes U)\eta_V^{-1}. Every internal contraction therefore becomes the original one.

The unit condition can be detected while both scalar Fock vacua remain fixed. In the K3 example, choose e=I−1(1)e=I^{-1}(1) and r1=1r_1=1. The transported distinguished vector is 1+p1+p. Keeping it incorrectly at 11 changes the quantum action on λ3q2(1)\lambda^3q_2(1) by λ2\lambda^2.

The distinguished vector, the algebra unit and the scalar Fock vacuum are separate data. This transport theorem compares supplied paired states. It does not identify independently constructed physical states or their actual units.

The cohomological and homological Hochschild comparisons also have different directions. Todd correction contracts polyvectors on the cohomological side and multiplies forms on the homological side. The normalized chain map In(a0[a1|⋯|an])=1n!a0da1∧⋯∧danI_n(a_0[a_1|\cdots|a_n]) =\frac1{n!}a_0\,da_1\wedge\cdots\wedge da_n satisfies IB=dIIB=dI, where BB is Connes’ cyclic operator. Its raw cochain counterpart preserves products through a homotopy. For X=∂xX=\partial_x, Y=∂yY=\partial_y, that homotopy is the unary differential operator XY/2XY/2. Cyclic trace normalization and supported chiral sewing require their own compatible maps.

Let EE be a nonzero finite graded vector space, and set A=End⁡(E)A=\operatorname{End}(E) with zero internal differential. Its normalized Hochschild chains are Cn(A)=A⊗(A/kI)⊗n.C_n(A)=A\otimes(A/kI)^{\otimes n}. The Hochschild boundary bb has homological degree minus one. Connes’ operator BB has degree one, with b2=B2=bB+Bb=0b^2=B^2=bB+Bb=0. These operators form a mixed complex.

Introduce uu of homological degree minus two. The negative-cyclic complex has differential D=b+uBD=b+uB on CCd−(A)=∏m≥0umCd+2m(A).CC^-_d(A)=\prod_{m\ge0}u^mC_{d+2m}(A). The product specifies the completion.

Supertrace gives a mixed chain map π:C∗(A)→k\pi:C_*(A)\to k. Choose a homogeneous basis vector of parity p0p_0, let ee project onto it, and put ε=(−1)p0\varepsilon=(-1)^{p_0}. The corner εe\varepsilon e has supertrace one, but B(e)=I[e]B(e)=I[e]. Its negative-cyclic lift therefore requires higher terms: 𝔠e(u)=e+∑m≥1(−1)m(2m)!m!um(e−I2)[e|⋯|e⏟2m].\mathfrak c_e(u)=e+ \sum_{m\ge1}(-1)^m\frac{(2m)!}{m!}\, u^m\left(e-\frac I2\right) [\underbrace{e|\cdots|e}_{2m}]. The recurrence of these coefficients gives D𝔠e=0D\mathfrak c_e=0.

Theorem

The maps π:CC∗−(A)→k[[u]],j(f)=εf𝔠e\pi:CC^-_*(A)\to k[[u]], \qquad j(f)=\varepsilon f\,\mathfrak c_e are continuous homotopy inverses. They preserve the nonnegative powers of uu.

Proof

Write xi=Ei0x_i=E_{i0}, yi=E0iy_i=E_{0i}. The matrix homotopy h(a0[a1|⋯|an])=∑ixi[yia0|a1|⋯|an]h(a_0[a_1|\cdots|a_n]) =\sum_i x_i[y_i a_0|a_1|\cdots|a_n] satisfies bh+hb=1−iπbh+hb=1-i\pi, where i(1)=εei(1)=\varepsilon e. The first face uses ∑ixiyi=I\sum_i x_iy_i=I. Internal faces cancel in pairs, and the graded cyclic face gives the supertrace term.

Put h~=∑m≥0(−uhB)mh,ℋ=h~(1−jπ).\widetilde h=\sum_{m\ge0}(-uhB)^m h, \qquad \mathcal H=\widetilde h(1-j\pi). Each coefficient uses finitely many chain operations. The mixed-complex identities give πj=1,Dℋ+ℋD=1−jπ.\pi j=1,\qquad D\mathcal H+\mathcal HD=1-j\pi. This proves both inverse identities on the completed complex.

For E=k1|1E=k^{1|1}, the two odd off-diagonal matrices satisfy [β,γ]gr=I[\beta,\gamma]_{\mathrm{gr}}=I. Thus I=b(β[γ])I=b(\beta[\gamma]), and the completed homotopy also gives a negative-cyclic primitive of II. The normalized class j(1)j(1) remains nonzero because its supertrace is one.

This does not make the matrix algebra acyclic: its internal differential is zero. The boundary occurs in its Hochschild complex. A degree-preserving strict mixed section exists precisely when the even and odd dimensions differ. In the balanced case the higher series supplies the inverse.

The normalized homological class ω=[εe]\omega=[\varepsilon e] also supports a specified rank-one Frobenius theory: ω⋆ω=ω,τ(ω)=1,Δω=ω⊗ω.\omega\star\omega=\omega,\qquad \tau(\omega)=1,\qquad \Delta\omega=\omega\otimes\omega. Its handle operator is the identity, and its connected correlators are products of the inserted scalars. Its Fock construction uses a separate Laurent variable and preserves the scalar vacuum.

The matrix comparison glues relatively over a commutative coefficient ring for a finite projective graded module with a specified even trivial summand. The finite dual-basis tensor defines the homotopy before completion.

Absolute coefficient operations remain additional. For R=k[x]R=k[x], the relative cyclic operator on RR over itself is zero. The absolute operator sends xx to 1[x]1[x], which the normalized Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg map sends to dxdx. Extending the relative matrix comparison to differential operators or supported chiral coefficients must preserve this operation, the topology and the geometric trace.

For an ordinary smooth variety, the combined homotopy calculus of Hochschild cochains and chains has a formality theorem, proved by Dolgushev, Tamarkin and Tsygan. Its ordinary smooth-variety domain remains distinct from the supported and completed coefficients required for the physical comparison.

36Hall flags and shuffle coefficients

Hall multiplication retains the geometry of extensions and their coefficients

Hall multiplication combines objects by forming extensions. Given functions f,gf,g on a category of objects, its quotient-first convention is (f∗g)(F)=∫U⊂Ff(F/U)g(U)dχc.(f*g)(F)=\int_{U\subset F}f(F/U)g(U)\,d\chi_c. The integral weights the actual subobject variety by compactly supported Euler characteristic. Iterated products count flags of subobjects, including their intermediate quotients. The unit is the function supported at the zero object.

This construction makes a geometric comparison possible when an equivalence preserves whole families of flags. A projective K3 surface supplies an explicit example. There is an ample class HH and three line bundles Li=𝒪(Di)L_i=\mathcal O(D_i) with H2=8,HDi=0,Di2=−8,DiDj=−4(i≠j).H^2=8,\qquad HD_i=0,\qquad D_i^2=-8,\qquad D_iD_j=-4\quad(i\ne j). Their common Hilbert polynomial is 4m2−24m^2-2. Each is stable, its self-extension dimensions in degrees 0,1,20,1,2 are (1,0,1)(1,0,1), and the cross-extension dimensions are (0,2,0)(0,2,0). Four boundary sectors carry the complete action

An order-three boundary permutation can solve the local mixed square by supplying the missing phase on three sectors. This preserves the pointed cube and both absorption cycles. Fixed sectors permit a complete action, but impose a sharp restriction.

Theorem

Let F:𝒞4I,4→MatB⁡(𝒞2I,2)F:\mathcal C_{4I,4}\to\operatorname{Mat}_B(\mathcal C_{2I,2}) be a linear strong marked action on a finite nonempty set BB, preserving the regular unit, pointed multiplication, all splitting maps and the specified source duality. Every entry of F(ρ4)F(\rho_4) is a sum of recipient invertibles. On each connected support component there are exactly two orbits of the source pointed group. The order-three label fixes one orbit and acts freely on the other. Each component therefore has at least four boundary indices.

The proof uses both fusion and duality. Write the positive-dimension matrix as A+dBτA+dB_\tau, where d=6+43d=6+4\sqrt3 and BτB_\tau counts recipient noninvertibles. Duality makes both matrices symmetric. On a component with tt pointed orbits, the fusion equation gives tr⁡(Bτ)=14(2−t).\operatorname{tr}(B_\tau)=14(2-t). The relative cubic equation makes this trace divisible by three. Nonnegativity forces t=2t=2, hence every diagonal noninvertible multiplicity is zero. The noninvertible coefficient of the full squared fusion equation then forces every off-diagonal multiplicity to vanish as well. If the two orbit sizes are r,sr,s, their remaining block multiplicities satisfy ru+sw=192,rs(v2−uw)=192.ru+sw=192,\qquad rs(v^2-uw)=192. The cubic divisibilities exclude two fixed orbits and two free orbits. One fixed orbit and one free orbit require at least 1+31+3 indices. The theorem concerns finite products of the stated recipient; it does not classify every intrinsic recipient module category.

An explicit separable algebra attains the bound. In the source group G=ℤ/24×ℤ/8G=\mathbb Z/24\times\mathbb Z/8, let H0={(3x,y):x,y∈ℤ/8}≃C8×C8,ψ((x,y),(x′,y′))=ξyx′,H_0=\{(3x,y):x,y\in\mathbb Z/8\}\simeq C_8\times C_8, \qquad \psi((x,y),(x',y'))=\xi^{yx'}, where ξ\xi is a primitive eighth root. It preserves all 192192 noninvertible splitting channels and both source duality maps. Its loop is d4d_4 on each regular matrix unit; it is not the ordinary trace of Y4Y_4. The arithmetic norm still needs its intermediate and duality comparisons

The marked network is an actual composite, 𝒩g=T0′T0′ρm(Tg)T0=bgidρm⁡,𝒩g𝒩0−1=wL(g,m)idρm⁡.\mathcal N_g=T'_0T'_0\rho_m(T_g)T_0 =b_g\operatorname{id}_{\rho_m},\qquad \mathcal N_g\mathcal N_0^{-1} =w_L(g,m)\operatorname{id}_{\rho_m}. Both full matrix actions preserve every constituent junction, hence this once-inserted operation. The inverse reference is a scalar line, not a tensor inverse of ρm\rho_m. Closing the network separately at every vertex would replace ww by wmw^m. If cc denotes the reference scalar at period one, the prescribed reference on an outer orbit of length ss is csc^s; finite matrix flattening does not change that normalization.

The pointed trace candidate has a label-level tower, but its object substitutions already disagree. Passing through the period-two root gives 261⊕︎14γ⊕︎56ρ126\,1\oplus14\,\gamma\oplus56\,\rho_1, whereas the direct root is 201⊕︎20γ⊕︎56ρ120\,1\oplus20\,\gamma\oplus56\,\rho_1. The difference is 6(1−γ)6(1-\gamma). These are proposed substitutions, not two existing tensor functors whose compositor has merely been omitted.

The extra duality junction supplies a separate comparison. With e=(1+i)/(1+3)e=(1+i)/(1+\sqrt3), the prescribed period-one tangle has value d1e=(3−2)(1+i).d_1e=(\sqrt3-2)(1+i). Identifying a source cup with that final cup after a scalar detector would leave ratios d2/d1=3−3d_2/d_1=3-\sqrt3 or d4/d1=36−203d_4/d_1=36-20\sqrt3. The objects Qr;tQ_{r;t} have the correct source loops, but this does not identify their junctions with those required by the final arithmetic tangle.

In the fixed relative field background W=VE8W=V_{E_8}, the constructed coefficient actions extend by 1W⊗κ1_W\otimes\kappa. Their position-independent maps commute with every finite principal part and normal derivative. They retain the ordered spectator and crossed coefficients FGF=FFGF=F and FGFG=EggFGFG=E_{gg} on the partitions 13|213|2 and 13|2413|24. The stated output completion and analytic convergence hypotheses remain necessary; arbitrary completed input states are not admitted.

The unresolved map is an operation-compatible arithmetic comparison to the actual intermediate recipient, with its receiver specified beyond these constructions. Strong regular descent and free cyclic finite-product realizations meet the stated obstructions; other module categories or nonlinear correspondences require their own maps. Such a comparison must preserve all fusion and duality junctions, the regular boundary unit, the normalized networks and the extra-junction tangle, and it must compare actual intermediate-period objects in a tower. The strict orbit transports and the full four-sector action establish positive constructions on their stated boundaries. They do not yet construct that arithmetic norm.
